title: Sample collection and scientific analyses to predict treatment response and side effects in CAR-T cell therapy
summary:
CAR (chimeric antigen receptor) T-cell therapy is a new and innovative treatment method, particularly for malignant diseases. Although the prospects for success are much better compared to conventional treatments, long-term (more than 2 years) disease-free survival has so far been observed in only about 40% of patients with lymphoma. 
Although the short-term side effects of this therapy are well known and, in some cases, easily managed, their occurrence cannot yet be predicted.
The aim of this study is to analyze specific proteins, cell types, genetic alterations, or pathogens (e.g., bacteria) using biological samples before and up to 10 years after CAR-T cell therapy in order to better understand and predict treatment response and the likelihood of (severe) side effects. To this end, findings collected as part of routine treatment will be included in the analysis.

interventions.name: Collection, analysis and storage of biosamples from patients before and up to 10 years after CAR-T cell therapy for malignant diseases

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Adult patients scheduled to undergo CAR-T cell therapy
- Malignant disease as the indication for CAR-T cell therapy
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of written consent from the patient
